audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for passion plot, Bethany anointing, Judas, Passover meal, covenant blood, Gethsemane, arrest, trial, Son of Humanity, Peter denial.

verses.restored: When Jesus finished all these words, he said to his disciples,

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said unto his disciples,

modern.text: When Jesus had finished saying all these things, He told His disciples,

original.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάντας τοὺς λόγους τούτους, εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: You know that after two days the Passover happens, and the Son of Humanity is handed over to be crucified.

familiar.text: Ye know that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified.

modern.text: “You know that the Passover is two days away, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”

original.text: Οἴδατε ὅτι μετὰ δύο ἡμέρας τὸ πάσχα γίνεται, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς τὸ σταυρωθῆναι.

verses.restored: Then the chief priests and elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest called Caiaphas,

familiar.text: Then assembled together the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders of the people, unto the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,

modern.text: At that time the chief priests and elders of the people assembled in the courtyard of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas,

original.text: Τότε συνήχθησαν οἱ ⸀ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως τοῦ λεγομένου Καϊάφα,

verses.restored: and took counsel together to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him.

familiar.text: And consulted that they might take Jesus by subtilty, and kill him.

modern.text: and they conspired to arrest Jesus covertly and kill Him.

original.text: καὶ συνεβουλεύσαντο ἵνα τὸν Ἰησοῦν δόλῳ κρατήσωσιν καὶ ἀποκτείνωσιν·

verses.restored: But they said, Not during the feast, lest an uproar happen among the people.

familiar.text: But they said, Not on the feast day, lest there be an uproar among the people.

modern.text: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.” Jesus Anointed at Bethany (Mark 14:3–9; Luke 7:36–50; John 12:1–8)

original.text: ἔλεγον δέ· Μὴ ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, ἵνα μὴ θόρυβος γένηται ἐν τῷ λαῷ.

verses.restored: When Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,

familiar.text: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,

modern.text: While Jesus was in Bethany in the home of Simon the Leper,

original.text: Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ γενομένου ἐν Βηθανίᾳ ἐν οἰκίᾳ Σίμωνος τοῦ λεπροῦ,

verses.restored: a woman came to him with an alabaster jar of very costly ointment, and she poured it on his head as he reclined.

familiar.text: There came unto him a woman having an alabaster box of very precious ointment, and poured it on his head, as he sat at meat.

modern.text: a woman came to Him with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, which she poured on His head as He reclined at the table.

original.text: προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ γυνὴ ⸂ἔχουσα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου⸃ βαρυτίμου καὶ κατέχεεν ἐπὶ ⸂τῆς κεφαλῆς⸃ αὐτοῦ ἀνακειμένου.

verses.restored: Seeing this, the disciples were indignant, saying, Why this waste?

familiar.text: But when his disciples saw it, they had indignation, saying, To what purpose is this waste?

modern.text: When the disciples saw this, they were indignant and asked, “Why this waste?

original.text: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ⸀μαθηταὶ ἠγανάκτησαν λέγοντες· Εἰς τί ἡ ἀπώλεια αὕτη;

verses.restored: For this could have been sold for much and given to the poor.

familiar.text: For this ointment might have been sold for much, and given to the poor.

modern.text: This perfume could have been sold at a high price, and the money given to the poor.”

original.text: ἐδύνατο γὰρ ⸀τοῦτο πραθῆναι πολλοῦ καὶ δοθῆναι πτωχοῖς.

verses.restored: Knowing this, Jesus said, Why do you trouble the woman? She has worked a beautiful/good work for me.

familiar.text: When Jesus understood it, he said unto them, Why trouble ye the woman? for she hath wrought a good work upon me.

modern.text: Aware of this, Jesus asked, “Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.

original.text: γνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί κόπους παρέχετε τῇ γυναικί; ἔργον γὰρ καλὸν ἠργάσατο εἰς ἐμέ·

verses.restored: For the poor you always have with you, but me you do not always have.

familiar.text: For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always.

modern.text: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.

original.text: πάντοτε γὰρ τοὺς πτωχοὺς ἔχετε μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν, ἐμὲ δὲ οὐ πάντοτε ἔχετε·

verses.restored: In pouring this ointment on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.

familiar.text: For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial.

modern.text: By pouring this perfume on Me, she has prepared My body for burial.

original.text: βαλοῦσα γὰρ αὕτη τὸ μύρον τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ σώματός μου πρὸς τὸ ἐνταφιάσαι με ἐποίησεν.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: wherever this good message is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be spoken in memory of her.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, there shall also this, that this woman hath done, be told for a memorial of her.

modern.text: Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.” Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus (Mark 14:10–11; Luke 22:3–6)

original.text: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅπου ἐὰν κηρυχθῇ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦτο ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ, λαληθήσεται καὶ ὃ ἐποίησεν αὕτη εἰς μνημόσυνον αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

familiar.text: Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests,

modern.text: Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

original.text: Τότε πορευθεὶς εἷς τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰούδας Ἰσκαριώτης, πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς

verses.restored: and said, What are you willing to give me, and I will hand him over to you? They weighed out thirty silver pieces to him.

familiar.text: And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.

modern.text: and asked, “What are you willing to give me if I hand Him over to you?” And they set out for him thirty pieces of silver.

original.text: εἶπεν· Τί θέλετέ μοι δοῦναι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν παραδώσω αὐτόν; οἱ δὲ ἔστησαν αὐτῷ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια.

verses.restored: From then he sought an opportune moment to hand him over.

familiar.text: And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.

modern.text: So from then on Judas looked for an opportunity to betray Jesus. Preparing the Passover (Mark 14:12–16; Luke 22:7–13)

original.text: καὶ ἀπὸ τότε ἐζήτει εὐκαιρίαν ἵνα αὐτὸν παραδῷ.

verses.restored: On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying, Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?

familiar.text: Now the first day of the feast of unleavened bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying unto him, Where wilt thou that we prepare for thee to eat the passover?

modern.text: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”

original.text: Τῇ δὲ πρώτῃ τῶν ἀζύμων προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ ⸀λέγοντες· Ποῦ θέλεις ⸀ἑτοιμάσωμέν σοι φαγεῖν τὸ πάσχα;

verses.restored: He said, Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, The Teacher says, My time is near; I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples.

familiar.text: And he said, Go into the city to such a man, and say unto him, The Master saith, My time is at hand; I will keep the passover at thy house with my disciples.

modern.text: He answered, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him that the Teacher says, ‘My time is near. I will keep the Passover with My disciples at your house.’”

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν πόλιν πρὸς τὸν δεῖνα καὶ εἴπατε αὐτῷ· Ὁ διδάσκαλος λέγει· Ὁ καιρός μου ἐγγύς ἐστιν· πρὸς σὲ ποιῶ τὸ πάσχα μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν μου.

verses.restored: The disciples did as Jesus instructed them, and they prepared the Passover.

familiar.text: And the disciples did as Jesus had appointed them; and they made ready the passover.

modern.text: So the disciples did as Jesus had directed them and prepared the Passover. The Last Supper (Mark 14:17–26; Luke 22:14–23; 1 Corinthians 11:17–34)

original.text: καὶ ἐποίησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὡς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἡτοίμασαν τὸ πάσχα.

verses.restored: When evening came, he reclined with the twelve.

familiar.text: Now when the even was come, he sat down with the twelve.

modern.text: When evening came, Jesus was reclining with the twelve disciples.

original.text: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἀνέκειτο μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα ⸀μαθητῶν

verses.restored: As they were eating, he said, Amen, I say to you: one of you will hand me over.

familiar.text: And as they did eat, he said, Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.

modern.text: And while they were eating, He said to them, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray Me.”

original.text: καὶ ἐσθιόντων αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι εἷς ἐξ ὑμῶν παραδώσει με.

verses.restored: They were deeply grieved, and each began to say to him, Surely not I, Lord?

familiar.text: And they were exceeding sorrowful, and began every one of them to say unto him, Lord, is it I?

modern.text: They were deeply grieved and began to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I, Lord?”

original.text: καὶ λυπούμενοι σφόδρα ἤρξαντο λέγειν αὐτῷ ⸂εἷς ἕκαστος⸃· Μήτι ἐγώ εἰμι, κύριε;

verses.restored: He answered, The one dipping his hand with me in the bowl, this one will hand me over.

familiar.text: And he answered and said, He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me.

modern.text: Jesus answered, “The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with Me will betray Me.

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ὁ ἐμβάψας μετʼ ἐμοῦ ⸂τὴν χεῖρα ἐν τῷ τρυβλίῳ⸃ οὗτός με παραδώσει·

verses.restored: The Son of Humanity goes as it has been written concerning him, but woe to that person through whom the Son of Humanity is handed over. It would have been beautiful/good for that person if he had not been born.

familiar.text: The Son of man goeth as it is written of him: but woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born.

modern.text: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed. It would be better for him if he had not been born.”

original.text: ὁ μὲν υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑπάγει καθὼς γέγραπται περὶ αὐτοῦ, οὐαὶ δὲ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐκείνῳ διʼ οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται· καλὸν ἦν αὐτῷ εἰ οὐκ ἐγεννήθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος.

verses.restored: Judas, the one handing him over, answered, Surely not I, Rabbi? He said to him, You have said it.

familiar.text: Then Judas, which betrayed him, answered and said, Master, is it I? He said unto him, Thou hast said.

modern.text: Then Judas, who would betray Him, said, “Surely not I, Rabbi?” Jesus answered, “You have said it yourself.”

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν εἶπεν· Μήτι ἐγώ εἰμι, ῥαββί; λέγει αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶπας.

verses.restored: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed, broke it, gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.

familiar.text: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body.

modern.text: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take and eat; this is My body.”

original.text: Ἐσθιόντων δὲ αὐτῶν λαβὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸀ἄρτον καὶ ⸀εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ⸂δοὺς τοῖς μαθηταῖς⸃ εἶπεν· Λάβετε φάγετε, τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ σῶμά μου.

verses.restored: Taking a cup and giving thanks, he gave it to them, saying, Drink from it, all of you.

familiar.text: And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it;

modern.text: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.

original.text: καὶ ⸀λαβὼν ποτήριον καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Πίετε ἐξ αὐτοῦ πάντες,

verses.restored: For this is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many for release of sins/misalignments.

familiar.text: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.

modern.text: This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

original.text: τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά ⸀μου ⸀τῆς διαθήκης τὸ περὶ πολλῶν ἐκχυννόμενον εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν·

verses.restored: I say to you: I will not drink from this fruit of the vine from now until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's reign.

familiar.text: But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.

modern.text: I tell you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father’s kingdom.”

original.text: λέγω δὲ ⸀ὑμῖν, οὐ μὴ πίω ἀπʼ ἄρτι ἐκ τούτου τοῦ γενήματος τῆς ἀμπέλου ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ὅταν αὐτὸ πίνω μεθʼ ὑμῶν καινὸν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρός μου.

verses.restored: After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

familiar.text: And when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives.

modern.text: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives. Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial (Zechariah 13:7–9; Mark 14:27–31; Luke 22:31–38; John 13:36–38)

original.text: καὶ ὑμνήσαντες ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν.

verses.restored: Then Jesus said to them, You will all stumble because of me this night; for it has been written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.

familiar.text: Then saith Jesus unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.

modern.text: Then Jesus said to them, “This very night you will all fall away on account of Me. For it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’

original.text: Τότε λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πάντες ὑμεῖς σκανδαλισθήσεσθε ἐν ἐμοὶ ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ταύτῃ, γέγραπται γάρ· Πατάξω τὸν ποιμένα, καὶ ⸀διασκορπισθήσονται τὰ πρόβατα τῆς ποίμνης·

verses.restored: But after I am raised, I will go before you to Galilee.

familiar.text: But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.

modern.text: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

original.text: μετὰ δὲ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με προάξω ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.

verses.restored: Peter answered, Even if all stumble because of you, I will never stumble.

familiar.text: Peter answered and said unto him, Though all men shall be offended because of thee, yet will I never be offended.

modern.text: Peter said to Him, “Even if all fall away on account of You, I never will.”

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ πάντες σκανδαλισθήσονται ἐν σοί, ⸀ἐγὼ οὐδέποτε σκανδαλισθήσομαι.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, Amen, I say to you: this night, before a rooster sounds, you will deny me three times.

familiar.text: Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.

modern.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus declared, “this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”

original.text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω σοι ὅτι ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με.

verses.restored: Peter said, Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you. All the disciples said likewise.

familiar.text: Peter said unto him, Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Likewise also said all the disciples.

modern.text: Peter replied, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” And all the other disciples said the same thing. Jesus Prays at Gethsemane (Mark 14:32–42; Luke 22:39–46)

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος· Κἂν δέῃ με σὺν σοὶ ἀποθανεῖν, οὐ μή σε ⸀ἀπαρνήσομαι. ⸀ὁμοίως καὶ πάντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν.

verses.restored: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane and said to the disciples, Sit here while I go there and pray.

familiar.text: Then cometh Jesus with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples, Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder.

modern.text: At that time Jesus went with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane, and He told them, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”

original.text: Τότε ἔρχεται μετʼ αὐτῶν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς χωρίον λεγόμενον Γεθσημανί, καὶ λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς· Καθίσατε αὐτοῦ ἕως οὗ ἀπελθὼν ⸂ἐκεῖ προσεύξωμαι⸃.

verses.restored: Taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be grieved and deeply distressed.

familiar.text: And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and very heavy.

modern.text: He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee and began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed.

original.text: καὶ παραλαβὼν τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς δύο υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου ἤρξατο λυπεῖσθαι καὶ ἀδημονεῖν.

verses.restored: Then he said to them, My soul/life is deeply grieved to the point of death; remain here and keep watch with me.

familiar.text: Then saith he unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me.

modern.text: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with Me.”

original.text: τότε λέγει ⸀αὐτοῖς· Περίλυπός ἐστιν ἡ ψυχή μου ἕως θανάτου· μείνατε ὧδε καὶ γρηγορεῖτε μετʼ ἐμοῦ.

verses.restored: Going forward a little, he fell on his face, praying, My Father, if possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will.

familiar.text: And he went a little farther, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.

modern.text: Going a little farther, He fell facedown and prayed, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me. Yet not as I will, but as You will.”

original.text: καὶ ⸀προελθὼν μικρὸν ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ προσευχόμενος καὶ λέγων· Πάτερ μου, εἰ δυνατόν ἐστιν, παρελθάτω ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦτο· πλὴν οὐχ ὡς ἐγὼ θέλω ἀλλʼ ὡς σύ.

verses.restored: He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, So, were you not strong enough to keep watch with me one hour?

familiar.text: And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour?

modern.text: Then Jesus returned to the disciples and found them sleeping. “Were you not able to keep watch with Me for one hour?” He asked Peter.

original.text: καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ εὑρίσκει αὐτοὺς καθεύδοντας, καὶ λέγει τῷ Πέτρῳ· Οὕτως οὐκ ἰσχύσατε μίαν ὥραν γρηγορῆσαι μετʼ ἐμοῦ;

verses.restored: Keep watch and pray, so that you may not enter testing. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.

familiar.text: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

modern.text: “Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”

original.text: γρηγορεῖτε καὶ προσεύχεσθε, ἵνα μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς πειρασμόν· τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής.

verses.restored: Again, a second time, he went and prayed, My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, let your will happen.

familiar.text: He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.

modern.text: A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done.”

original.text: πάλιν ἐκ δευτέρου ἀπελθὼν προσηύξατο λέγων· Πάτερ μου, εἰ οὐ δύναται ⸀τοῦτο ⸀παρελθεῖν ἐὰν μὴ αὐτὸ πίω, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου.

verses.restored: Again he came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.

familiar.text: And he came and found them asleep again: for their eyes were heavy.

modern.text: And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping—for their eyes were heavy.

original.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν ⸂πάλιν εὗρεν αὐτοὺς⸃ καθεύδοντας, ἦσαν γὰρ αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ βεβαρημένοι.

verses.restored: Leaving them again, he went away and prayed a third time, saying the same word again.

familiar.text: And he left them, and went away again, and prayed the third time, saying the same words.

modern.text: So He left them and went away once more and prayed a third time, saying the same thing.

original.text: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς ⸂πάλιν ἀπελθὼν⸃ προσηύξατο ἐκ τρίτου τὸν αὐτὸν λόγον εἰπὼν ⸀πάλιν.

verses.restored: Then he came to the disciples and said, Sleep the rest and rest? Look, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Humanity is handed over into sinners' hands.

familiar.text: Then cometh he to his disciples, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

modern.text: Then He returned to the disciples and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is near, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

original.text: τότε ἔρχεται πρὸς τοὺς ⸀μαθητὰς καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Καθεύδετε ⸀τὸ λοιπὸν καὶ ἀναπαύεσθε· ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ἡ ὥρα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοται εἰς χεῖρας ἁμαρτωλῶν.

verses.restored: Rise, let us go. Look, the one handing me over has drawn near.

familiar.text: Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that doth betray me.

modern.text: Rise, let us go! See, My betrayer is approaching!” The Betrayal of Jesus (Mark 14:43–52; Luke 22:47–53; John 18:1–14)

original.text: ἐγείρεσθε ἄγωμεν· ἰδοὺ ἤγγικεν ὁ παραδιδούς με.

verses.restored: While he was still speaking, look, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and elders of the people.

familiar.text: And while he yet spake, lo, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and elders of the people.

modern.text: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a large crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests and elders of the people.

original.text: Καὶ ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ Ἰούδας εἷς τῶν δώδεκα ἦλθεν καὶ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ὄχλος πολὺς μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων ἀπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τοῦ λαοῦ.

verses.restored: The one handing him over had given them a sign, saying, Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him.

familiar.text: Now he that betrayed him gave them a sign, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he: hold him fast.

modern.text: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς σημεῖον λέγων· Ὃν ἂν φιλήσω αὐτός ἐστιν· κρατήσατε αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Immediately he came to Jesus and said, Greetings, Rabbi, and kissed him.

familiar.text: And forthwith he came to Jesus, and said, Hail, master; and kissed him.

modern.text: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed Him.

original.text: καὶ εὐθέως προσελθὼν τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπεν· Χαῖρε, ῥαββί· καὶ κατεφίλησεν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, Friend, do what you came for. Then they came and laid hands on Jesus and seized him.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto him, Friend, wherefore art thou come? Then came they, and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.

modern.text: “Friend,” Jesus replied, “do what you came for.” Then the men stepped forward, seized Jesus, and arrested Him.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἑταῖρε, ἐφʼ ⸀ὃ πάρει. τότε προσελθόντες ἐπέβαλον τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: And look, one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.

familiar.text: And, behold, one of them which were with Jesus stretched out his hand, and drew his sword, and struck a servant of the high priest’s, and smote off his ear.

modern.text: At this, one of Jesus’ companions drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ εἷς τῶν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπέσπασεν τὴν μάχαιραν αὐτοῦ καὶ πατάξας τὸν δοῦλον τοῦ ἀρχιερέως ἀφεῖλεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτίον.

verses.restored: Then Jesus said to him, Return your sword to its place, for all who take the sword will perish by the sword.

familiar.text: Then said Jesus unto him, Put up again thy sword into his place: for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword.

modern.text: “Put your sword back in its place,” Jesus said to him. “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.

original.text: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀπόστρεψον ⸂τὴν μάχαιράν σου⸃ εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς, πάντες γὰρ οἱ λαβόντες μάχαιραν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ⸀ἀπολοῦνται·

verses.restored: Or do you think I cannot call on my Father, and he will now place beside me more than twelve legions of messengers?

familiar.text: Thinkest thou that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels?

modern.text: Are you not aware that I can call on My Father, and He will at once put at My disposal more than twelve legions of angels?

original.text: ἢ δοκεῖς ὅτι οὐ ⸀δύναμαι παρακαλέσαι τὸν πατέρα μου, καὶ παραστήσει μοι ⸂ἄρτι πλείω⸃ δώδεκα λεγιῶνας ἀγγέλων;

verses.restored: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?

familiar.text: But how then shall the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be?

modern.text: But how then would the Scriptures be fulfilled that say it must happen this way?”

original.text: πῶς οὖν πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ ὅτι οὕτως δεῖ γενέσθαι;

verses.restored: In that hour Jesus said to the crowds, Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs to arrest me? Day by day I sat teaching in the temple, and you did not seize me.

familiar.text: In that same hour said Jesus to the multitudes, Are ye come out as against a thief with swords and staves for to take me? I sat daily with you teaching in the temple, and ye laid no hold on me.

modern.text: At that time Jesus said to the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw? Every day I sat teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me.

original.text: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς ὄχλοις· Ὡς ἐπὶ λῃστὴν ἐξήλθατε μετὰ μαχαιρῶν καὶ ξύλων συλλαβεῖν με; καθʼ ⸀ἡμέραν ⸂ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐκαθεζόμην διδάσκων⸃ καὶ οὐκ ἐκρατήσατέ με.

verses.restored: All this happened so that the writings of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples left him and fled.

familiar.text: But all this was done, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples forsook him, and fled.

modern.text: But this has all happened so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples deserted Him and fled. Jesus before the Sanhedrin (Mark 14:53–65; Luke 22:66–71; John 18:19–24)

original.text: τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῶσιν αἱ γραφαὶ τῶν προφητῶν. τότε οἱ μαθηταὶ πάντες ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἔφυγον.

verses.restored: Those who seized Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders were gathered.

familiar.text: And they that had laid hold on Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were assembled.

modern.text: Those who had arrested Jesus led Him away to the house of Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.

original.text: Οἱ δὲ κρατήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήγαγον πρὸς Καϊάφαν τὸν ἀρχιερέα, ὅπου οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι συνήχθησαν.

verses.restored: Peter followed him from far away to the courtyard of the high priest, entered, and sat with the attendants to see the end.

familiar.text: But Peter followed him afar off unto the high priest’s palace, and went in, and sat with the servants, to see the end.

modern.text: But Peter followed Him at a distance, right up to the courtyard of the high priest. And he went in and sat down with the guards to see the outcome.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἕως τῆς αὐλῆς τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, καὶ εἰσελθὼν ἔσω ἐκάθητο μετὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν ἰδεῖν τὸ τέλος.

verses.restored: The chief priests and the whole council sought false witness against Jesus so they might put him to death,

familiar.text: Now the chief priests, and elders, and all the council, sought false witness against Jesus, to put him to death;

modern.text: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking false testimony against Jesus in order to put Him to death.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς ⸀καὶ τὸ συνέδριον ὅλον ἐζήτουν ψευδομαρτυρίαν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὅπως ⸂αὐτὸν θανατώσωσιν⸃,

verses.restored: but they found none, though many false witnesses came. Later two came forward

familiar.text: But found none: yea, though many false witnesses came, yet found they none. At the last came two false witnesses,

modern.text: But they did not find any, though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward

original.text: καὶ οὐχ εὗρον ⸂πολλῶν προσελθόντων ψευδομαρτύρων. ὕστερον δὲ προσελθόντες δύο⸃

verses.restored: and said, This one said, I am able to destroy the temple of the Divine and through three days rebuild it.

familiar.text: And said, This fellow said, I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days.

modern.text: and declared, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’”

original.text: εἶπαν· Οὗτος ἔφη· Δύναμαι καταλῦσαι τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν ⸀οἰκοδομῆσαι.

verses.restored: The high priest stood and said to him, Do you answer nothing? What are these testifying against you?

familiar.text: And the high priest arose, and said unto him, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee?

modern.text: So the high priest stood up and asked Him, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”

original.text: καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνῃ; τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;

verses.restored: But Jesus was silent. The high priest said, I adjure you by the living Divine: tell us whether you are the Messiah, the Son of the Divine.

familiar.text: But Jesus held his peace. And the high priest answered and said unto him, I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us whether thou be the Christ, the Son of God.

modern.text: But Jesus remained silent. Then the high priest said to Him, “I charge You under oath by the living God: Tell us if You are the Christ, the Son of God.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐσιώπα. ⸀καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐξορκίζω σε κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος ἵνα ἡμῖν εἴπῃς εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, You have said it. Yet I say to you: from now you will see the Son of Humanity sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto him, Thou hast said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall ye see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.

modern.text: “You have said it yourself,” Jesus answered. “But I say to all of you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Σὺ εἶπας· πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπʼ ἄρτι ὄψεσθε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενον ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.

verses.restored: Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, He blasphemed. What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy.

familiar.text: Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He hath spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now ye have heard his blasphemy.

modern.text: At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “He has blasphemed! Why do we need any more witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy.

original.text: τότε ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς διέρρηξεν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ⸀λέγων· Ἐβλασφήμησεν· τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν μαρτύρων; ἴδε νῦν ἠκούσατε τὴν ⸀βλασφημίαν·

verses.restored: What do you think? They answered, He is liable to death.

familiar.text: What think ye? They answered and said, He is guilty of death.

modern.text: What do you think?” “He deserves to die,” they answered.

original.text: τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ; οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν· Ἔνοχος θανάτου ἐστίν.

verses.restored: Then they spat in his face and struck him; others slapped him,

familiar.text: Then did they spit in his face, and buffeted him; and others smote him with the palms of their hands,

modern.text: Then they spit in His face and struck Him. Others slapped Him

original.text: τότε ἐνέπτυσαν εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκολάφισαν αὐτόν, οἱ δὲ ἐράπισαν

verses.restored: saying, Prophesy to us, Messiah. Who struck you?

familiar.text: Saying, Prophesy unto us, thou Christ, Who is he that smote thee?

modern.text: and said, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who hit You?” Peter Denies Jesus (Mark 14:66–72; Luke 22:54–62; John 18:15–18)

original.text: λέγοντες· Προφήτευσον ἡμῖν, χριστέ, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε;

verses.restored: Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and one servant girl came to him, saying, You also were with Jesus the Galilean.

familiar.text: Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee.

modern.text: Meanwhile, Peter was sitting out in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him. “You also were with Jesus the Galilean,” she said.

original.text: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ⸂ἐκάθητο ἔξω⸃ ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ· καὶ προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ μία παιδίσκη λέγουσα· Καὶ σὺ ἦσθα μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Γαλιλαίου·

verses.restored: But he denied it before all, saying, I do not know what you mean.

familiar.text: But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest.

modern.text: But he denied it before them all: “I do not know what you are talking about.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο ⸀ἔμπροσθεν πάντων λέγων· Οὐκ οἶδα τί λέγεις.

verses.restored: When he went out to the gate, another saw him and said to those there, This one was with Jesus the Nazarene.

familiar.text: And when he was gone out into the porch, another maid saw him, and said unto them that were there, This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth.

modern.text: When Peter had gone out to the gateway, another servant girl saw him and said to the people there, “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth.”

original.text: ἐξελθόντα ⸀δὲ εἰς τὸν πυλῶνα εἶδεν αὐτὸν ἄλλη καὶ λέγει ⸀τοῖς ἐκεῖ· ⸀Οὗτος ἦν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου·

verses.restored: Again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.

familiar.text: And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.

modern.text: And again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the man!”

original.text: καὶ πάλιν ἠρνήσατο μετὰ ὅρκου ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

verses.restored: After a little while, those standing came and said to Peter, Truly you also are one of them, for even your speech makes you clear.

familiar.text: And after a while came unto him they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art one of them; for thy speech bewrayeth thee.

modern.text: After a little while, those standing nearby came up to Peter. “Surely you are one of them,” they said, “for your accent gives you away.”

original.text: μετὰ μικρὸν δὲ προσελθόντες οἱ ἑστῶτες εἶπον τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ἀληθῶς καὶ σὺ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ, καὶ γὰρ ἡ λαλιά σου δῆλόν σε ποιεῖ·

verses.restored: Then he began to curse and swear, I do not know the man. Immediately a rooster sounded.

familiar.text: Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.

modern.text: At that he began to curse and swear to them, “I do not know the man!” And immediately a rooster crowed.

original.text: τότε ἤρξατο καταθεματίζειν καὶ ὀμνύειν ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον. καὶ ⸀εὐθέως ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν·

verses.restored: Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken, Before a rooster sounds, you will deny me three times. Going outside, he wept bitterly.

familiar.text: And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.

modern.text: Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.” And he went outside and wept bitterly.

original.text: καὶ ἐμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τοῦ ⸀ῥήματος Ἰησοῦ ⸀εἰρηκότος ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με, καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἔξω ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς.
